headline: Five Governments Open Rwanda Return-Hub Talks
deck: The planned pilot targets people without a right to remain, while five governments say concrete negotiations will begin.
body: Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands are expected to open a Rwanda return hub ready to accept transfers in 2027, Dutch and Danish government statements said. [E5] The planned offshore centre is expected to face legal challenges and has been denounced as a grave moral failing, the Guardian reported. [E1] Their joint statement said concrete negotiations with Rwanda would begin for implementation. [E2]

Yesterday, Austria’s Interior Ministry said it was holding confidential talks with several possible partner countries. [E10] The announcement identifies Rwanda as the partner for the planned hub. [E2]

The scheme would apply to adults whose asylum claims have been rejected or who otherwise have no legal right to live in the European Union. [E4] The BBC said the scheme differs from the scrapped British plan, which would have sent people to Rwanda to have their claims processed. [E7]
Officials hope to send 100 people to Rwanda from early next year to test the model. [E3] Dutch and Danish government statements said the hub was expected to be ready to accept transfers in 2027. [E5]

People sent to Rwanda could integrate there or return to their home country, the nations said. [E6] Austrian Chancellor Christian Stocker said the countries sought to relieve European asylum systems and stop traffickers arranging Mediterranean crossings. [E8]

Human Rights Watch’s senior Africa researcher Clementine de Montjoye said Rwanda’s support for armed rebels in neighbouring Democratic Republic of Congo, alongside its record on repression, detention and treatment in detention, made the choice a concern. [E9]
